p: Born about 1487, Nuno da Cunha was the son of Antónia Pais and of Tristão da Cunha, the navigator, admiral and ambassador to Pope Leo X. He first proved himself in the fighting at Oja and Brava and at the capture of Panane, under the viceroy Francisco de Almeida. King John III of Portugal, to whom he had been close since the king was a prince, named him ninth governor of the Portuguese possessions in India, with orders to end the government of Lopo Vaz de Sampaio and send him to Portugal in chains.

The pirates he subdued at Mombasa on the passage out had been harassing the coast of Portuguese Mozambique, whose watering stations were essential to the route to western India. His brothers Pero Vaz da Cunha and Simão da Cunha were to have served as his second and third in command, as was expected in the Estado da Índia, but both died on the voyage, and during his long rule he had to rely on local networks of clientage in Goa. He took office in April 1529 and held it for nine years, longer than any other governor of Portuguese Asia in the sixteenth century.

In 1529 he sent an expedition that sacked and burned Damão in Gujarat. On 20 January 1533 forces under his control captured Baxay, the later Bassein and present Vasai, from Bahadur Shah. The next year it became the capital of the Portuguese province of the North, and its citadel of black basalt was begun; the citadel was completed in 1548 and still stands. In 1538 an army of the Sultanate of Gujarat under Khadjar Safar, aided by Ottoman forces, besieged the Portuguese in Diu.

Court intrigues forced his return to Portugal. He was shipwrecked at the Cape of Good Hope on the way and drowned; his death is dated 5 March 1539. He had married first Maria da Cunha and then Isabel da Silveira. The main source for his career is the history of the Portuguese in the East by João de Barros, who lived from 1496 to 1570.

notes: Short article (about 400 words): the entry is at the low end.

The article says he was 'shipwrecked at the Cape of Good Hope and drowned'; the existing entry says he 'died at sea on the voyage home'. Not contradictory, but the editor may want to check the shipwreck.
The article gives no year for the Mombasa action and does not mention the 1535 fortress at Diu that the existing entry has; I did not repeat or date them.
'present Vasai': the article says 'Baxay (now Vasai ...)', 'renamed Bassein'.
